name: Segmental Arterial Mediolysis

criteria.description: Histopathological evidence of segmental lysis of the arterial media with absence of inflammation
Angiographic demonstration of arterial aneurysms, dissections, or stenoses predominantly in splanchnic or cerebral arteries
Exclusion of inflammatory vasculitis and other mimicking conditions by clinical, laboratory, and imaging studies
Acute abdominal pain or neurological deficits related to arterial rupture or ischemia

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation plus characteristic angiographic findings with exclusion of vasculitis
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is often retrospective after surgical or autopsy specimen analysis; imaging is critical for clinical suspicion.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Segmental arterial medial necrosis without inflammation
searchTerms: artery wall muscle death without inflammation

pathognomonic.symptomName: Splanchnic artery aneurysms with risk of rupture
pathognomonic.notes: Commonly involves celiac, mesenteric, or renal arteries

common.symptomName: Acute abdominal pain due to arterial dissection or rupture
searchTerms: sudden belly pain from artery rupture
acute abdominal pain from vessel tear

common.symptomName: Hypertension secondary to renal artery involvement
searchTerms: high blood pressure from kidney artery
secondary high blood pressure from kidneys

common.symptomName: Neurological deficits from cerebral artery involvement
common.notes: Includes transient ischemic attacks or strokes
searchTerms: brain nerve problems from artery disease
neurological deficits from brain artery issues

occasional.notes: Secondary to abdominal ischemia or hemorrhage

occasional.symptomName: Back pain related to retroperitoneal hemorrhage
searchTerms: lower back pain from bleeding behind abdomen
back pain due to internal bleeding

occasional.notes: Possible inflammatory response despite absence of vasculitis

rare.notes: Less commonly involved than splanchnic arteries
searchTerms: swollen blood vessels in arms or legs

rare.notes: Due to renal artery dissection or occlusion

searchTerms: weakness on one side of body

laboratory: Normal inflammatory markers (CRP, ESR) despite arterial injury
Absence of autoantibodies typical for vasculitis
imaging: Angiography showing segmental arterial aneurysms, dissections, stenoses
CT angiography demonstrating arterial wall irregularities and hemorrhage
genetic: No known genetic mutations currently associated
other: Histopathology revealing segmental lysis of arterial media without inflammatory infiltrate

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of systemic inflammation and necrotizing vasculitis
Non-inflammatory arterial stenosis with characteristic 'string of beads' appearance
Lack of medial lysis and hemorrhage
Risk factors such as hyperlipidemia and smoking
Gradual onset without acute arterial wall lysis

redFlags: Sudden onset of severe abdominal pain indicating possible arterial rupture
Signs of intra-abdominal hemorrhage or shock
Neurological deficits suggestive of cerebral artery involvement
references: Slavin RE, et al. Segmental arterial mediolysis: a clinical pathologic study. Human Pathology. 1976.
Boyer L, et al. Segmental arterial mediolysis: a rare cause of abdominal aneurysms. Ann Vasc Surg. 2019.
